caseStudies.title: App Map - Homelab Dashboard
caseStudies.excerpt: A modern homelab dashboard for managing and monitoring self-hosted applications with health checks, categories, and Uptime Kuma integration.
caseStudies.challenge: Managing a growing homelab with dozens of self-hosted applications became chaotic. Bookmarks scattered across browsers, no unified health monitoring, and no easy way to know which services were up or down. I needed a single dashboard to organize and monitor everything.
caseStudies.solution: Built App Map - a clean, modern dashboard that catalogs all homelab applications with health status monitoring. Each app can be categorized, tagged, and configured with custom health checks. Integration with Uptime Kuma provides robust monitoring data. The dashboard supports both local and remote URLs for access from anywhere.
caseStudies.developmentProcess: Started with the TanStack Start template and built incrementally. Designed the database schema first (lesson learned from previous projects), then built the CRUD operations, followed by the health check system. Added Uptime Kuma integration last as an enhancement.
caseStudies.technicalImplementation: TanStack Start with React 19 for the full-stack framework. Better Auth for authentication. PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM for data persistence. Health checks run on configurable intervals with support for HTTP, TCP, and Uptime Kuma monitors. Widget system for at-a-glance status information.
caseStudies.results: All homelab apps now accessible from one dashboard. Health status visible at a glance. Categories keep services organized. Notes feature allows documentation of each service's purpose and configuration. Grid and list views accommodate different preferences.
caseStudies.lessonsLearned: Starting with proper authentication from day one saved refactoring later. The widget system was added after realizing I wanted quick status info without scrolling. Integration with existing tools (Uptime Kuma) is more valuable than rebuilding monitoring from scratch.

caseStudies.title: OmniChat - AI-Powered Live Chat Widget
caseStudies.excerpt: A self-hosted live chat widget with AI-powered responses using local Ollama models, real-time admin dashboard, and webhook integrations.
caseStudies.challenge: Wanted a way for portfolio visitors to ask questions without relying on third-party chat services that track users or require monthly subscriptions. The chat needed to handle common questions automatically while allowing human takeover for complex inquiries.
caseStudies.solution: Built OmniChat - a self-hosted live chat system with three components: an embeddable widget for any website, a real-time admin dashboard, and an AI backend powered by Ollama. The AI handles initial responses using context about AppaHouse, while humans can take over any conversation.
caseStudies.developmentProcess: Built the Socket.io server first to handle real-time communication. Added the visitor widget as a lightweight embeddable component. Built the admin dashboard for monitoring and responding to chats. Integrated Ollama for AI responses with streaming support. Added webhooks for notifications.
caseStudies.technicalImplementation: Express server with Socket.io for real-time bidirectional communication. Ollama integration for local AI inference with streaming responses. Session management with visitor tracking. Rate limiting and security headers. Webhook notifications for new sessions. Admin authentication with JWT tokens.
caseStudies.results: Visitors can get immediate answers to common questions. AI responses are contextual and helpful. Admins receive webhook notifications for new chats. All data stays self-hosted - no third-party tracking. Lightweight widget loads quickly on any page.
caseStudies.lessonsLearned: Streaming AI responses provides much better UX than waiting for complete responses. Socket.io makes real-time features surprisingly simple. Rate limiting is essential from day one to prevent abuse. Context files for AI should be kept concise and focused.

caseStudies.title: Indigo Sun Florals E-Commerce Platform
caseStudies.excerpt: A modern e-commerce platform for locally sourced flower arrangements with inventory management and subscription capabilities.
caseStudies.challenge: Indigo Sun Florals needed a way to sell locally sourced flower arrangements that vary by season and availability. The challenge was to create a system that could handle dynamic inventory, custom arrangements, and provide a subscription model to increase customer retention and predictable cash flow.
caseStudies.solution: Built a full-featured e-commerce website with real-time inventory display, custom arrangement builder, and subscription management system. The platform allows customers to browse available stock, create custom arrangements, and subscribe for recurring deliveries based on seasonal availability.
caseStudies.developmentProcess: Applied lessons from earlier projects where I rushed into coding without proper planning. This time, I started with database schema design and authentication, then built the product catalog system, followed by the shopping cart and checkout flow. Final phase included the subscription system and admin dashboard.
caseStudies.technicalImplementation: React 19 with the new React Compiler for optimal performance. TanStack Start provided the full-stack framework with server-side rendering and API routes. Drizzle ORM with PostgreSQL handled complex inventory queries and transaction management. Better Auth provided secure authentication with role-based access control.
caseStudies.results: The platform achieved a 40% increase in customer retention through the subscription model, 65% improvement in click-through rates compared to the previous solution, and streamlined the payment process resulting in 30% faster checkout times. Inventory management became 50% more efficient with real-time updates.
caseStudies.lessonsLearned: Taking time to properly design the database schema upfront saved significant refactoring time later - a lesson I learned the hard way on previous projects. The subscription model proved more valuable than anticipated. Previous mistakes with state management taught me to plan data flow carefully.

caseStudies.title: AIDJ - AI-Assisted Music Library
caseStudies.excerpt: A self-hosted music library interface with Navidrome integration, featuring a comprehensive CI/CD pipeline built from lessons learned in version control.
caseStudies.challenge: Managing a self-hosted music library lacked a modern, intuitive interface. More importantly, my earlier projects suffered from poor testing practices and messy deployments. I wanted to build something that showcased better development practices I'd learned through trial and error.
caseStudies.solution: Built AIDJ - a modern web dashboard integrating with Navidrome for music library management and streaming. Critically, I implemented a comprehensive CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions, including automated testing, security scanning with Trivy, and 80%+ code coverage requirements.
caseStudies.developmentProcess: This project represented a turning point in my development practices. After dealing with deployment issues and bugs that slipped through on earlier projects, I set up CI/CD from day one. Every commit triggers automated tests, security scans, and coverage checks before merging.
caseStudies.technicalImplementation: React 19 with React Compiler for optimal rendering. TanStack ecosystem (Start, Router, Query) for full-stack capabilities. Navidrome API integration with proper error handling and fallbacks. CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions: Trivy security scanning, Vitest for unit tests, and enforced 80%+ code coverage.
caseStudies.results: Successfully deployed a privacy-focused music interface running entirely on local infrastructure. The CI/CD pipeline has caught multiple issues before they reached production - something my earlier projects lacked. Sub-100ms response times with seamless music browsing.
caseStudies.lessonsLearned: Setting up comprehensive CI/CD early pays enormous dividends. Previous projects taught me the pain of manual testing and deployments. Integrating with third-party APIs requires careful error handling - I learned this the hard way. The extra time spent on testing infrastructure saved countless hours debugging production issues.

caseStudies.title: Minecraft Server List Platform
caseStudies.excerpt: A comprehensive Minecraft server listing platform with fair ranking, real-time server status, voting system, 'I'm Feeling Lucky' discovery, and admin moderation.
caseStudies.challenge: Existing Minecraft server list platforms often use unfair ranking systems that favor paid promotions over quality servers. The community needed a transparent, fair platform. For me, this was also a chance to apply everything I'd learned from previous projects and mistakes.
caseStudies.solution: Built a complete server listing platform with a multi-factor ranking algorithm that considers votes, uptime, player activity, and freshness. Implemented real-time server pinging using minecraft-protocol, user voting system with rate limiting, comprehensive analytics dashboard, and full admin panel. Added 'I'm Feeling Lucky' for random server discovery and server age badges.
caseStudies.developmentProcess: This project benefited from all my previous experiences. Database schema was designed upfront (lesson from Indigo Sun). CI/CD was set up from day one (lesson from AIDJ). Role-based access control was planned before coding (lesson from multiple projects). Background jobs were architected properly (avoiding past mistakes with real-time features).
caseStudies.technicalImplementation: TanStack Start with Nitro runtime for server-side rendering and API routes. Multi-factor ranking algorithm with configurable weights for fair rankings. minecraft-protocol library for accurate server status pinging. Scheduled background jobs for health checks. Better Auth with role-based access control. Resend for transactional emails. Recharts for analytics. Toast notifications for better UX feedback. Loading skeletons for perceived performance.
caseStudies.results: Platform provides fair, transparent server rankings based on actual metrics. Real-time server status updates every 5-15 minutes. Comprehensive analytics help server owners understand their traffic. 'I'm Feeling Lucky' feature encourages discovery of lesser-known servers. Server age badges build trust. The cleanest codebase I've shipped, reflecting accumulated learning.
caseStudies.lessonsLearned: Multi-factor ranking algorithms require careful weight tuning - I had to iterate several times to get fair results. Background job scheduling is critical for real-time features. Rate limiting is essential for voting systems (learned from early abuse attempts). Small UX touches like loading skeletons and toast notifications make a big difference. This project showed me how much I've grown as a developer.

caseStudies.title: Housekeeping Scheduler
caseStudies.excerpt: A schedule management application that solved a real workplace problem, teaching me the value of user-focused development.
caseStudies.challenge: Managing housekeeping schedules with spreadsheets was error-prone and time-consuming. This was one of my first projects solving a real problem for real users, which meant learning to prioritize features based on actual needs rather than technical interest.
caseStudies.solution: Built a purpose-built scheduling application with CSV import/export capabilities, drag-and-drop schedule management, and real-time updates. The focus was on solving the immediate problem rather than adding unnecessary features.
caseStudies.developmentProcess: Rapid prototyping approach with continuous user feedback. This taught me the value of showing work early and iterating based on real usage. Started with core scheduling UI, then added features users actually requested - not features I thought were cool.
caseStudies.technicalImplementation: React with TypeScript for type-safe development. shadcn/ui components for consistent, accessible UI. Vite for fast development and optimized builds. Express backend for API endpoints. Docker deployment with Cloudflare Tunnel for secure remote access.
caseStudies.results: Reduced schedule management time by 60%. CSV import eliminates manual data entry errors. Real-time updates ensure all staff see current schedules. Most importantly, users actually use it daily - validation that solving real problems matters more than technical perfection.
caseStudies.lessonsLearned: Domain-specific tools dramatically improve efficiency over generic solutions. User feedback is more valuable than my assumptions. Docker deployment simplifies hosting and updates - I wish I'd learned this earlier. Shipping something useful beats shipping something perfect.
